title: Physically Isolated Deployment Intake - Pioneer Cardiology
summary: Discovery call for a physically isolated on-prem inference deployment. Discussed no-network update processes, signed firmware/tooling, GPU footprint constraints, SSO and audit requirements, and a pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: share private deployment checklist, cost estimate for 1x rack (A100 equivalent) + ops runbook, and schedule a hands-on networked benchmark in a staging room window.
next_steps: Samira to send private deployment checklist + draft pricing by 2025-09-19
Daniel to prepare a short hw compatibility matrix and recommended quant profiles by 2025-09-24
Schedule pilot kickoff: 2 week window week of 2025-10-06 - Samira to propose times
action_items: Samira Khan: share deployment-checklist.pdf and initial pricing (due 2025-09-19)
Daniel Hsieh: hardware compatibility matrix + quantization notes (due 2025-09-24)
Lucas Reed: provide rack PDU/PSU limits and current GPU model list (due 2025-09-20)
Aisha Gomez: send SOC2 cert snapshot and list of mandatory controls for audit (due 2025-09-22)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-17 15:00 PDT | Duration 54m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel, Lucas Reed, Aisha Gomez, Tom Becker

[00:00] Samira (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 55 minutes. quick intros?
[00:07] Dr. Maya Patel: hi, maya here. i'm leading our clinical ML efforts at Pioneer Cardiology. we've been evaluating LLM features for triage notes and report summarization.
[00:14] Lucas Reed: lucas, infra, i run the data center side and manage on-prem clusters.
[00:18] Aisha Gomez: aisha, ciso. i'll be driving compliance and vendor security gating.
[00:22] Samira: great thanks. i'll let daniel introduce from the tech side and then we'll jump into constraints.
[00:27] Daniel (SE): hey all, daniel, i'm the systems engineer. i've done a handful of private deployments. quick note — we try to map the deployment to three buckets: hosted, dedicated, private/physically isolated. you're obviously in the third.
[00:39] Tom Becker: quick thing — our facility is completely isolated, no outbound internet for inference nodes, updates are via removable media and a guarded jump box. we need to make sure the model and runtime updates fit that model.
[00:49] Daniel (SE): understood. two main patterns we've done: signed artifact bundles with offline key injection via HSM or a physically escorted HSM device, or a jumpbox controlled by your ops team that pulls from a sealed staging VM. both require a signing workflow and chain-of-custody documentation.
[01:05] Aisha: chain-of-custody is key. we can't have unsigned binaries touching any node. does redwood support signed model bundles and offline key injection?
[01:12] Samira: yes — we support signed bundles and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key provisioning. the on-prem control plane can be configured to accept only signed images, and we provide an attestation checklist.
[01:21] Lucas: hardware — we have a single rack allocated, 2x 3U chassis, older PSUs, and thermal headroom is limited. current GPUs are a mix — one set of A40s and a couple of older V100s. what's your recommended footprint for a baseline?
[01:36] Daniel (SE): for production with reasonable latency for short prompts, we usually recommend at least an A100-equivalent per model shard. given PSU limits and thermals, we can map to A40s with quantized runtimes — that will reduce accuracy slightly but cut power and memory needs. we can run a profiling pass to estimate tokens/sec.
[01:50] Dr. Maya: accuracy drift is a concern for clinical tasks. how much does quantization change outputs? do you run evals tied to prompt sets?
[01:57] Daniel (SE): yes, redwood optimize workflows include prompt-set evals and regression alerts. we can recommend quant profiles with thresholds (e.g. int8 + fisher calibration) and provide examples where accuracy drop is <2% for summarization tasks. but we'll surface where it's risky.
[02:13] Aisha: audit logging — we require immutable logs, per-request traceability, and retention for 7 years for certain flows. can you describe your logging footprint on private?
[02:23] Samira: on private, logs are stored locally to your syslog/ELK stack or to your on-prem audit store; we can ship in structured JSON and include token-level cost breakdown if you want. retention and immutability are controlled by your storage. we also support signed audit bundles for export.
[02:38] Lucas: update cadence — we plan quarterly model refreshes and emergency security patches maybe monthly. how are you handling rollback in an air-gapped setup?
[02:48] Daniel (SE): typical pattern: we stage both new and canary runtimes as signed artifacts; the control plane verifies signatures then runs a health check on a isolated canary node. rollback is handled by re-signing the older artifact as the active image or by keeping immutable images and toggling active pointers in the control plane. offline, that toggle is performed via the jumpbox operator with an audit trail.
[03:06] Tom: does redwood's console still exist in private? like dashboards and tracing?
[03:10] Samira: we ship a private console that runs in your network. it has the same UI but can be configured to only accept internal access. streaming telemetry can be routed to your observability stack; nothing needs to leave the facility.
[03:21] Aisha: SSO — we use SAML via the hospital SSO. must be integrated.
[03:25] Daniel (SE): supported. we can federate via your identity provider, or if truly air-gapped, we can use certificate-based auth and an on-prem LDAP cache. we also support RBAC and token scoping for per-route controls.
[03:39] Dr. Maya: governance — who owns model updates? our clinical team needs sign-off; can we gate deploys until a clinical signer approves?
[03:46] Samira: yes, we can implement approval gates. deploys can be paused until an approver signs off. we can also enable canary rollouts limited to a small instance pool for clinical review.
[03:58] Lucas: networking question — we have a strict egress policy. the nodes cannot make any outbound connections except to an internal control plane. how does your routing/fallback work during capacity constraints?
[04:09] Daniel (SE): locally hosted private deployments don't rely on Redwood hosted fallback by default. we can design fallback policies that use a standby model variant in the same network. if you want cross-site failover, we'd need a secure replicator over an air-gapped transfer process (sneakernet or physically transported media) and explicit operational runbooks.
[04:26] Aisha: compliance — we need evidence of secure build pipelines and deterministic builds. do you provide SBOMs and build attestations?
[04:33] Samira: yes, for private we provide SBOMs, build attestations, and signed artifact manifests. we can also integrate with your CI signing process so the artifacts are verifiable end-to-end.
[04:44] Dr. Maya: pilot scope — we want a single model for note summarization, limited to cardiology notes, with a weekly update cadence for the first month, then move to quarterly. minimal latency requirement is sub-1s for 50-token prompts. is that realistic on our hardware?
[05:00] Daniel (SE): sub-1s on mixed A40/V100 will be tough. with aggressive quantization and a tuned runtime we might hit ~1-1.5s median. to reliably hit sub-1s we'd recommend at least one A100-class GPU or a smaller model variant optimized for latency. we can profile with a representative corpus in a staging window.
[05:17] Lucas: i'll pull exact GPU serials and PDU limits and send them.
[05:20] Samira: perfect — that's one of the action items. we'll need the exact rack topology to size us.
[05:24] Aisha: about keys — we require keys never be exported in plaintext. we prefer an HSM that stays offline and a signing token handed to an operator. is that workable?
[05:33] Daniel (SE): totally. we've worked with YubiHSM and on-prem Thales modules. the signing operation happens in the HSM; only the signature leaves. for key injection we support in-person ceremonies and come with HSM integration guides.
[05:46] Dr. Maya: what about model updates for clinical validation? we need a parallel validation env that mirrors prod but with smaller footprint. can redwood run a validation pipeline offline?
[05:55] Samira: yes, we can package a validation harness that runs locally. results can be exported as signed reports and stored in your validation archive.
[06:04] Tom: procurement — budget asks, are you able to provide a seat license or is it usage-based?
[06:09] Samira: for private deployments typically we do a platform subscription + annual support and an ops fee. we can propose both a capacity-based (per-GPU) and a flat platform license. we'll include both in the pricing doc.
[06:20] Lucas: timeline — we'd like to pilot in October, with production by Q1 2026. any blockers?
[06:26] Daniel (SE): blockers are: hw power/thermals, chain-of-custody process for updates, and clinical acceptance testing. none are showstoppers, just operational.
[06:35] Aisha: one more — vulnerability management. we need a process for critical CVEs that can be patched without online access. what's redwood's emergency patch story?
[06:42] Daniel (SE): we support emergency signed patches; our incident response team will prepare signed artifacts and a step-by-step offline patch runbook. we can also offer remote guidance over an escorted phone/video session during the patch window.
[06:56] Samira: okay, quick recap and next steps. samira: we'll send the private deployment checklist and pricing by friday (2025-09-19). daniel will share a hardware compatibility matrix and quantization recommendations. lucas will send rack and GPU specifics. aisha will forward compliance controls. we'll aim to lock a pilot window first week of october.
[07:16] Dr. Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:20] Samira: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invite and checklist.
[07:24] Meeting end.
